If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The failure occurs in the test `testPrefixMapClear` where a prefixMap view of a PatriciaTrie is cleared via prefixMap.clear(). The reported bug is a NullPointerException thrown on this clear(). The workaround to remove items one by one by the remove method works without an exception.

From the `prefixMap(String key)` method in AbstractPatriciaTrie, we see it delegates to `getPrefixMapByBits(K key, int offsetInBits, int lengthInBits)`.

This method returns a new PrefixRangeMap instance if the prefix length is non-zero.

PrefixRangeMap is a nested class holding the prefix, offsetInBits, and lengthInBits.

The bug happens on clear() on the PrefixRangeMap instance, so likely the PrefixRangeMap class has a clear method forwarding calls or implementing clear directly.

The NullPointerException suggests that some state needed to clear within the PrefixRangeMap is null or uninitialized or the clear method implementation is not handling its internal logic correctly.

The removals by remove method working indicates that remove is correctly implemented or delegated to the primary trie, while clear has an issue.

We have seen there is ambiguity between the clear() methods in various nested classes like EntrySet.clear(), Values.clear(), KeySet.clear(), and the main AbstractPatriciaTrie.clear().

Since PrefixRangeMap is a SortedMap, its clear probably overrides clear in some subclass.

The problem likely is that the clear method on the PrefixRangeMap does not properly remove all mapped entries or tries to operate on some internal data structure that may be null or broken when viewed through the prefixMap.

The cause is: clear method on PrefixRangeMap throws NPE because it attempts to modify the main PatriciaTrie structural data but fails due to missing initialization or incorrect implementation.

The remove method works however because it likely forwards each remove call individually and does not trigger the same failing code path.

Hence, the diagnosis is: In AbstractPatriciaTrie, the PrefixRangeMap implementation fails in the clear() method due to an attempt to directly clear the underlying data structure incorrectly or with a null reference, causing NullPointerException.

The fix needs investigation and correction of PrefixRangeMap.clear() method to correctly remove all entries with that prefix in the main trie without NPE.

# Final Diagnosis

The NullPointerException on clear() of the prefixMap is caused by an incorrect or incomplete implementation of the clear() method in AbstractPatriciaTrie.PrefixRangeMap. This method attempts to clear all entries mapped by the prefix range but interacts with internal data structures incorrectly, causing a null pointer exception. The remove method works fine because it removes entries one by one, avoiding the broken code path. The fix requires correcting the clear() method in AbstractPatriciaTrie.PrefixRangeMap to safely and correctly clear all prefix entries in the trie.

---

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
